back: One item of data stored about every record; a column of the table, with a name and a data type.
All the data stored about one item (one entity occurrence); a row of the table.
A field whose value is unique for every record, so it identifies each record.

front: The six basic data types for database fields
back: Text/alphanumeric, character, Boolean, integer, real, date/time.

front: Data type for a telephone number
back: Text: it keeps the leading zero, spaces and + sign, and no arithmetic is done on it.

front: Why store a date of birth instead of an age?
back: An age changes every year and would need updating; the age can be calculated from the date of birth, which never changes.
A rule applied as data is entered that rejects values that are not sensible or allowed, e.g. a range, presence, length, type or format check.
A pattern that controls the characters that may be typed into a field, position by position (e.g. a letter then four digits).
Format changes how a stored value is displayed; an input mask controls what may be typed in.
